activities.name: Agency formulation

BR-2028-0042 · draft v1

## Context

The agency identifies a flood-damaged bridge on a federal road and requests $10 million for a bridge-repair program. The request explains the need, proposed work, and estimated cost.

## Sample record

- **Budget year:** FY 2028
- **Program:** Flood-Damaged Bridge Repair
- **Requested:** $10,000,000
- **Priority site:** Cedar Creek Bridge · fictional

Restore a flood-damaged federal-road crossing used by school buses and emergency vehicles. Request condition-based repairs, design support, and access planning.

## Package contents

- Justification narrative — Word / PDF-style working document
- Estimate workbook — Spreadsheet / budget-table extract
- Leadership briefing — Presentation outline

activities.name: OMB review and passback
activities.example: OMB reviews the $10 million request and asks the agency to revise its repair priorities and delivery schedule. The agency submits an updated request; this is still planning for proposed funding.
activities.example_document: OMB passback and versioned agency response

artifact.title: Passback decision memo
artifact.format: OMB communicates budget decisions and direction; the agency may appeal and later receives settlement guidance. Formats vary. This sample uses a memo and revision table.
decisions: Retain the proposed $10 million program level.
Put routes serving essential access first.
Replace uniform allowances with condition-based estimates and show quarterly phasing.
artifact.body: Agency response v2: revised the bridge priority list and cost schedule; added quarterly phasing. This planning exchange does not enact an appropriation.
artifact.source_label: Example agency passback and settlement process

PB-2028-017 · pre-decisional sample

## Context

OMB reviews the $10 million request and asks the agency to revise its repair priorities and delivery schedule. The agency submits an updated request; this is still planning for proposed funding.

## Sample record

- **To:** Agency budget director
- **From:** OMB budget review · sample
- **Planning level:** $10,000,000 proposed

Agency response v2: revised the bridge priority list and cost schedule; added quarterly phasing. This planning exchange does not enact an appropriation.

## Passback directions

- **Funding level:** Retain the proposed $10 million program level.
- **Priorities:** Put routes serving essential access first.
- **Revision requested:** Replace uniform allowances with condition-based estimates and show quarterly phasing.

activities.name: President’s budget
activities.example: The President’s budget proposes $10 million for the bridge-repair program and is transmitted to Congress. The proposal does not itself provide spending authority.

artifact.title: President’s budget — program excerpt
artifact.format: Published budget tables and supporting narratives. This is a small program-level excerpt from a much larger submission.
artifact.body: The Administration proposes a bridge-repair program focused on restoring essential access. The request includes project prioritization and expected delivery milestones. Congress will consider funding through legislation.

activities.name: Congressional consideration

activities.name: Apportionment
activities.example: OMB approves a $2.5 million apportionment for the period, subject to its conditions. The approved schedule links this limit to the original $10 million appropriation.

artifact.title: Apportionment schedule — simplified
artifact.format: A resource-and-period schedule approved by OMB. This preview simplifies the fields; it is not a reproduction of an official form.
artifact.body: The current period’s limit is linked to the appropriation and its conditions. Funds-control records retain the approved schedule and subsequent changes.

activities.name: Allotment
activities.example: The agency allots $1 million of the apportioned $2.5 million to the district responsible for the bridge. The district’s allotment and its restrictions are recorded in the funds-control system.

artifact.title: Allotment decision
artifact.format: An agency applies its funds-control rules and records an allotment. The decision tree makes that reasoning visible in this example.
artifact.body: The approved $1 million allotment goes to the district responsible for Cedar Creek Bridge. The remaining $1.5 million is available for other allotments in this simplified scenario.

decision.question: Does the $1 million request fit the available amount, purpose, and approval conditions?
decision.no: Return for review; no allotment recorded

# Allotment decision

> Fictional sample for the Budget Atlas prototype. Not an official document.

AL-001 · agency funds control

## Context

The agency allots $1 million of the apportioned $2.5 million to the district responsible for the bridge. The district’s allotment and its restrictions are recorded in the funds-control system.

## Sample record

- **Parent:** AP-001 · $2,500,000
- **District request:** $1,000,000

The approved $1 million allotment goes to the district responsible for Cedar Creek Bridge. The remaining $1.5 million is available for other allotments in this simplified scenario.

## Decision flow

AP-001: $2.5 million apportioned

Does the $1 million request fit the available amount, purpose, and approval conditions?

- Yes: Record AL-001: $1 million allotted
- No: Return for review; no allotment recorded

$1.5 million remains unallotted

activities.name: Obligations and commitments
activities.example: After the necessary reviews, the district signs a $750,000 bridge-repair contract. The agency records this obligation against the $1 million allotment.

artifact.title: Contract and obligation record
artifact.format: The signed contract is supported by an obligation entry in the financial system. This is an invented screen, not an integration.
artifact.body: The contract file includes approvals and the evidence supporting the obligation. The recorded amount stays within the approved allotment.

OB-001 · sample financial-system screen

## Context

After the necessary reviews, the district signs a $750,000 bridge-repair contract. The agency records this obligation against the $1 million allotment.

## Sample record

- **Contract:** BR-12-2028 · Cedar Creek Bridge
- **Scope:** Deck repair and abutment stabilization
- **Source allotment:** AL-001 · $1,000,000
- **Recorded obligation:** $750,000
- **Unobligated allotment:** $250,000

The contract file includes approvals and the evidence supporting the obligation. The recorded amount stays within the approved allotment.

activities.name: Disbursements
activities.example: Engineers accept the first stage of work, and an approved invoice results in a $500,000 payment through Treasury. The contract still has $250,000 obligated but unpaid.
activities.example_document: Acceptance record, approved invoice, and payment receipt

artifact.format: Acceptance documentation and an approved invoice support a payment record. The display is illustrative.
artifact.body: The agency accepts the work and approves the invoice. The financial system records the payment and retains its Treasury reconciliation reference.

activities.name: Closeout and audit
activities.example: Later, after the remaining work and final $250,000 payment are complete, staff reconcile the contract and retain its audit trail. The appropriation account closes under its own availability and cancellation rules.

artifact.title: Closeout and reconciliation note
artifact.format: Project reconciliation and audit evidence are retained together. Appropriation-account closeout follows its own applicable rules.
artifact.body: After final acceptance and the remaining payment, staff reconcile the contract and retain the approval trail. Unused allotment and account balances are addressed under the applicable funds-control and account-closeout rules.

## Context

Later, after the remaining work and final $250,000 payment are complete, staff reconcile the contract and retain its audit trail. The appropriation account closes under its own availability and cancellation rules.

timeframe: Follow one funding request through enactment, execution, and closeout. Appropriations have different availability periods, and their lifecycle can span multiple fiscal years.
